title: Cedric Wiefel
text:
I am currently exploring opportunities where I can apply and learn more about causal inference.
I hold a Master of Science in Statistics from the University of Copenhagen. A big part of my master’s, more than half, was spent studying causal discovery and causal inference. Before that, I obtained a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from the University of Bonn with a focus on numerical mathematics and statistics.
Outside of academia, I enjoy demanding sports, as they provide a good balance to theoretical work and help me stay motivated and maintain a strong work ethic. I competed in fencing for over ten years and attended a sports high school. I also enjoy reading classic literature, baking, and cooking with friends.
On this website, I share what I am currently working on, what I have been working on in the past, and what I am interested in.

Research Interest
I recently completed a master’s degree in Statistics and have a strong background in simulation studies, machine learning, and mathematics. My interests lie in causal inference and its theoretical foundations, particularly targeted maximum likelihood estimation and semiparametric efficiency theory. I am motivated by developing advanced statistical methods and applying them to complex real-world problems, while communicating insights through effective visualisations and clear scientific writing.

title: Cedric Wiefel
text:
Research interests

Causal inference Assumptions and study design Semiparametric theory Nonparametric statistics TMLE DML Heterogeneous treatment effects Tree-based methods Ensemble methods Online experimentation

Broadly, I am interested in causal inference and issues that arise when applying causal inference methods. More specifically, I am interested in assumption violations and how different study designs rely on different sets of assumptions to obtain valid causal estimates.
In the context of estimation, I find semiparametric theory compelling. I more drawn to targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE), while also being interested in double/debiased machine learning (DML).
Besides biostatistics and economics, two prominent fields of application for causal inference, I am also looking to explore online experimentation, including A/B testing.
As causal inference is a relatively young field, it offers many opportunities for methodological advances and for integrating causal methods into a wide range of other fields. In the longer term, I hope to pursue research that involves these developments and their applications. Overall, I see causal inference as a means of better understanding and modelling the world and thereby answering important questions.
